root_idea.summary: The core lexical orientation is the grape and its vine, alongside several independently lexicalized formations associated with or homonymous to this basic word.
root_idea.development: The primary noun denotes the grape fruit and, by an attested extension, the grapevine itself. Related formations describe producing or possessing grapes, grape-related qualities, and a range of separate Classical Arabic objects and epithets.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The canonical Quranic nominal is presented under the normalized citation form عِنَب.

senses.definition: Grapes, the fruit of the grapevine.
senses.usage_conditions: The fruit term is applied to fresh grapes; an individual berry is عِنَبَةٌ, while dried grapes are separately called زَبِيب.
This plant sense occurs in descriptions of vineyards, gardens, and cultivated land; the same noun therefore denotes either the vine or its fruit according to context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce grapes, said of a grapevine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Derived Form II verb; the attested use describes the vine's production rather than an independently stated causative object.
A dialectal, non-Quranic extension attributed to the dialect of Yemen.
The unit noun corresponding to عِنَب; its plural of paucity is عِنَبَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small painful pustule that swells and may emit blood or fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also applied to such a lesion occurring in the eye or throat.
An attributive adjective derived from the grape term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet for a male gazelle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Traditional explanations vary between brisk or lively, sluggish, or advanced in age; the form is also reported with the plural عُنْبَانٌ.
A separate animal application of the same lexical form, without a corresponding verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The foremost portion or leading surge of a torrent, or the foremost part of a company of men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Variant forms include عُنْبَبٌ.
A separate Classical Arabic use of the same noun.
A rare identification reported in the lexical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large or conspicuously ugly nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet applied to a man; the related expression أَعْنَبُ الأَنْفِ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female genital part, or the portion excised from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical use with variant lexical explanations in the sources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small or high isolated mountain or hill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions vary: small and black, erect and sharp-headed, round, or barren; the form is also given with the plural عُنْبٌ.
An occupational noun formed from عِنَب.
The term is also reported for the fruit of the arak and for the fruit or tree called غُبَيْرَاء; it is a noun of unity with ة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman's fingers or fingertips, by comparison with red jujubes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on resemblance in color and form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Jujube-colored or the color of the jujube fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the colloquial phrase صَبَغَ الكِيسَ عُنَّابِيّ, the expression means that a person became bankrupt.
A possessive adjective patterned like لَابِنٌ, “possessing milk,” and تَامِرٌ, “possessing dates.”
An epithet applied to a man.
A separate adjectival use applied to the consistency of tar.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Verb meaning: a grapevine produces grapes.
Fruit meaning and its individual-berry term are represented.
Vine sense explicitly associated with Quranic usage.
Dialectal wine extension is kept outside the Quranic senses.
Forepart of a torrent or company.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the mountain/nose entry.

cautions: The Quranic vine sense is distinct from the fruit sense; contextual translations may render the same underlying noun as either grapes or grapevines.
Several rare Classical Arabic derivatives have variant or competing traditional explanations, which are retained in their usage conditions rather than treated as Quranic meanings.
